invalid_failure_risks: Internal contradiction in branching condition: blueprint says '(windowIndex & 0x80) !== 0' (fires at index >= 128) but also says 'windowIndex % 43 === 0' (fires at 43, 86 which are < 128) — these are mutually exclusive; test indices 43 and 86 would not trigger the bitwise condition, making those test cases ineffective or breaking the environment build

Both bugs are findable by cross-file grep/source reading without experimental instrumentation, undermining the 'no_repro_given' lever and making the task more like a 20-command read-and-fix than a genuinely exploratory debugging challenge

Timing-dependent flakiness in timestamp boundary test: if the test framework synthesizes window_start timestamps at exactly 500ms before a second boundary, the result depends on how state.json timestamps are seeded — a race between system clock and test setup could make this test non-deterministic
The hkdf npm package API (parameter order for salt/info) may not match blueprint assumptions, causing the manual HKDF verification test to fail for environment reasons rather than solver error

Sample windows 0-14 cover indices 0-14, all < 43, so the modulo-43 branching condition never fires in samples — this is consistent, but the dashboard showing windows 3, 7, 11 failing contradicts the modulo-43 claim (3, 7, 11 are not multiples of 43)
review.reasons: The blueprint has a critical internal contradiction: the branching condition is described as both '(windowIndex & 0x80) !== 0' (fires at index >= 128) and 'windowIndex % 43 === 0' (fires at 43, 86), but these are mutually exclusive, and neither explains why sample windows 3, 7, 11 fail (none are >= 128 or multiples of 43). This inconsistency makes the environment impossible to build correctly and renders several tests invalid. Additionally, both bugs are discoverable by source reading and a cross-file grep in ~20 commands, so the genuine difficulty is lower than the 'hard' rating implies.
fixes: Resolve the branching condition contradiction: choose ONE consistent condition (e.g., windowIndex >= 128 OR windowIndex % 43 === 0) and ensure the sample window failure pattern (windows 3, 7, 11 failing) is consistent with it — e.g., if using a % 4 === 3 condition, windows 3, 7, 11 fail cleanly

To increase genuine difficulty, move the branching condition into a shared utility that's imported by both session_key_manager.js and verifier.js, so the fix requires understanding the import graph rather than just grepping two files — and make the Math.round/floor bug appear only in a helper function with an innocuous name like 'normalizeEpoch'

Add a third subtle bug (e.g., off-by-one in window index passed to HKDF info when log_rotator.js increments before vs after encryption) to make the fuzz test harder to pass with a partial fix, and ensure the sample logs' failure pattern is mathematically consistent with the actual branching condition used
